PREMISE CORRECTION, and it is the one the orchestrator should read first: S60's factual premise about pair03 does not survive being measured. The ruling says pair03 'went from a uniformly lit flat olive ground with no shadow anywhere to a large soft cast shadow with sunlit patches'. My shadow-map ablation mask says the crop was ALREADY 68.75%-77.88% cast shadow BEFORE the change; the area rose only to 76.93%-79.23%. Every one of the sixteen 32-row bands of that crop got DARKER (top band -32.07 luma, bottom -16.49); 90.61% of its pixels got darker and 8.70% brighter. What F4 did at pair03 was not put the window into shadow — it REMOVED THE FILL LIGHT THAT WAS MAKING THE EXISTING SHADOW LEGIBLE, and M6 agrees: retention 0.7199 -> 0.4526 full frame (0.4202 -> 0.2693 on the builder's own crop, through the hard-fail line) and C_shadow 9.762 -> 4.785, through the exterior_daylight minimum of 6. S60's GENERAL RULE — an ablation metric is only valid on the support of the thing ablated — is sound and I applied it. Its APPLICATION to F4 ('the acceptance is met in substance') was ruled on a description of two frames that the pixels do not support, and measuring it S60's own way does not rescue pair03.

BRIEF CORRECTION: my dispatch said the build 'visibly regresses a third' recipe. It does not. dusk-canopy is byte-untouched and its capture is BIT-IDENTICAL (same SHA-256) between my two source trees. The -28% luma / -40% chroma / p10 -> 0.00 numbers belong to a REFUSED candidate arm, which I reproduced exactly (38.358 -> 27.724, 22.002 -> 13.112, p10 8.99 -> 0.00). Leaving a recipe alone after measuring that the obvious change breaks it, and writing the measurement into the source file, is correct engineering and should not be scored as a regression.

biggest_gap.what: F4 bought cast-shadow visibility by cutting the light that fills shadows, and it raised a key that is the same colour as everything else. Two measurements, one cause. (1) At pair03 — the window the piece itself presents as its result — cast-shadow area rose (68.75% -> 76.93% at tau=8) while M6 `retention` fell 0.7199 -> 0.4526 and M6 `C_shadow` fell 9.762 -> 4.785, through RI-VIS03's exterior_daylight minimum of 6. On the builder's own banked judged crop `retention` falls 0.4202 -> 0.2693, THROUGH the 0.30 hard-fail line RI-VIS03 labels 'crushed blacks / no ambient / no IBL'. Open `frames/pair03__BEFORE-sourcerevert__AFTER__AFTER-shadowmap-OFF.png`: the third panel is the same frame with the shadow map switched off and it is fully sunlit, so the whole window is genuinely in the building's shadow — and the middle panel shows there is now nothing to see inside it. (2) M6 `hue_offset`, which RI-VIS04 §2 names as its DETECT and RI-VIS03 calls the one-number test for 'a single white DirectionalLight plus a white AmbientLight', reads 3.72 deg on the landed build against a 6 deg hard-fail line and a 15 deg minimum, while six vendored modern-fidelity plates measured on the same instrument in the same session read 16.06 to 143.28 deg. F4 moved it by +0.49 deg. This is also, independently, the verbatim complaint of all five Protocol A r2 judges: 'every surface returns the same flat matte olive-grey'.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: F4 exists because three green visual fixes moved no human judgement. This one moves real quantities — the key IS dominant now at four of five windows, and there IS more cast-shadow area everywhere. But the two things the judges actually named are hue separation and readable occlusion, and on the corpus's own metrics for both, the frame after F4 is still a one-light frame with holes in it. A fourth round that adds more key without fixing the fill and the colour will spend against an instrument we can already show does not predict the judgement.

remedy.action: Two levers, both already in the file, neither of which F4 used. (1) `noon-marsh` declares `keyWarmth: 0.0`. It is a LIVE lever — sky.js:815-816 lerps the sun colour toward the horizon for positive values and the zenith for negative — and dusk-canopy uses 0.85, overcast-flat -0.30, night-moon -0.80. Warm the noon key (start at +0.45) and cool the fill, so lit and shadowed surfaces stop returning the same hue. (2) The env cut from 1.00 to 0.35 was applied as a flat scalar; the shadowed side is exactly where it was doing useful work. Either restore env toward ~0.55-0.65 and take the key dominance back from `sky`/`fill` instead, or add a dedicated shadow-fill term, and re-measure. BOTH must be measured at the same windows in the same run, because they trade against each other: warming the key raises hue_offset and raising env lowers the key ratio.
remedy.acceptance: AT THE SAME FIVE JUDGED WINDOWS, ALL THREE, and paired per S59 so neither can be bought with the other: (i) M6 `hue_offset` >= 6.0 deg in every daylight window, which is only the hard-fail line and not yet the 15 deg bar — say so; (ii) M6 `retention` >= 0.60 and M6 `C_shadow` >= 6 in every window whose cast-shadow area rose, measured on the FULL FRAME and on the sealed crop; (iii) S60 clause (a) — lit-subset key_off >= 2x env_off — must NOT fall at any window that already passes it (pair01 3.32/3.12, pair02 5.58/3.55, pair04-crop 5.49, pair05 4.45/4.83 are the numbers to hold), and clause (b) cast-shadow area must not fall. Every number from `tools/visual/f4c-critic.mjs --mode s60` against a SOURCE-LEVEL revert, not a page-side rig edit.

secondary_observations: COVERAGE IS WORSE THAN THE PIECE OR STATUS.md SAYS, AND IN A DIRECTION NEITHER NAMES. Transcribing the arithmetic out of sky.js apply() and recipeForConditions() and evaluating it at one-minute resolution: in clear weather night-moon holds 48.54% of the clock (18:11-05:50), noon-marsh 44.93% (06:37-17:24) and dusk-canopy 6.53% (05:50-06:37 and 17:24-18:11). The builder and STATUS.md both state the dusk band as 'roughly 05:20-06:40 and 17:20-18:40' — wrong at both ends, because recipeForConditions() tests `night > 0.55` FIRST. 94 minutes a day, not ~160. But recipe selection tests WEATHER before it tests the hour, and neither document costs it: computing each region's stationary weather distribution from game/data/world/weather.json and mapping the states through sky.js's own WEATHER table, `overcast-flat` or `storm` — both untouched and both unmeasured, still carrying env 1.10 and 1.15 against noon-marsh's new 0.35 — are selected for 59.1% of daylight averaged over the thirteen regions, from 19.8% in The Hive to 100% in The Deep Marshes and 79.7% in Blackwood. So the rebalance reaches roughly 35.7% of daylight. STATUS.md names the 6.5% omission and not the 59.1% one.

THE DUSK BAND IS QUANTIFIED, NOT JUST NAMED: at prsv-dusk (06:00, dusk-canopy) the lit-subset key/env ratio is 0.128 after and 0.135 before — unchanged, and failing the 2.0 bar by a factor of 15. That is what 'still carries the old flat look' means as a number.

sd_luma AS A 'NOT FLATTER' METRIC: the builder's CONCLUSION is right and its stated RULE is not. Across all ten shipped/key_off pairs in its own banked data, switching the key off RAISES sd at pair01 (+6.7%, +7.0%, +18.8%), pair05 (+2.9%, +5.5%) and deep night (+6.5%), and LOWERS it at pair02 (-61.8%), pair03 (-9.4%, twice) and pair04 (-67.7%). It rises in exactly the windows containing sky (pair01 sky fraction 0.048) and falls in the crops that do not (pair03 0.004, pair04 0.000). So sd_luma there is the sky-to-ground ratio, as the builder said — and 'switching the key off raises it' holds in 3 of 7 windows, not universally. The conclusion that matters survives intact: a preservation metric that can improve when the key is switched off cannot be used to protect the key.

corpus_extended.what: §3 gains two clauses, `§3-D2` and `§3-D3`. Nothing was removed and no threshold was lowered.
corpus_extended.why: §3's existing DETECT reads 'M6 SHADOW_MASK fraction < 3% in a daylight exterior = no shadows'. That test CANNOT detect the absence of shadows: RI-VIS03 §0 defines SHADOW_MASK as the darkest QUARTILE of the foreground by construction, so it is ~25% of the foreground whether the scene casts one shadow or none. Measured across ten frames of this build, before and after a change that demonstrably added cast-shadow area, SHADOW_MASK frac sat between 0.2329 and 0.2498 in EVERY ONE. The clause can only fire when the sky fills >88% of the frame. Same misdomained-metric family as S58, S59 and S60. §3-D2 replaces it with a shadow-map ablation mask reported as a curve over tau; §3-D3 adds the preservation clause this verdict's biggest gap demonstrates the need for — a build can add shadow area by deleting the light that fills shadows.
corpus_extended.bound: Both clauses are DETECT and preservation only. They add no route to a higher §14 mark and no route to a higher score for any build; a critic may cite them to WITHHOLD a mark and never to grant one. Overturned if a shadow-map ablation proves unavailable to a harness, in which case §3 falls back to the penumbra and cascade-ring tests and records the area clause UNVERIFIED, which counts as absent.
corpus_extended.note: CRITIC-DOCTRINE §1.3 forbids an extension being the reason a critic PASSES. This verdict's status is FAIL and neither added clause contributes to it: the FAIL is set by S60 clause (a), which predates me, and by RI-VIS04 §2's OWN pre-existing DETECT. §3-D2 is the one clause on which the build PASSES, and it lifts nothing because the score is a min.

arbitration_questions.question: S60 clause (b) is 'the cast-shadow area fraction does not fall in any window'. At pair05 (19:30, night-moon) `sky.js:645` sets `moon.castShadow = false`, so the directional key that carries the frame CANNOT cast a shadow and the measured area is 0.02%-0.30% in both arms — the clause is being evaluated on noise. Is clause (b) DEGENERATE on any window whose key cannot cast a shadow, and should it therefore be recorded `inapplicable` rather than passed or failed? I have recorded it `inapplicable` and said so, which is the fail-closed reading only if the answer is also that a shadowless night is itself a defect — which I believe it is, and which the builder names as the obvious next thing at night.

S60 says 'in all five windows' and does not name a DOMAIN. Measured on the lit subset, the build passes 4 of 5 on the sealed 512x512 judged crop (pair03 fails) and 4 of 5 on the full 1920x1080 frame (pair04 fails) — the same split as the unrepaired metric, at better absolute numbers. I have ruled that clause (a) is NOT MET because no single domain passes all five and choosing per window would be metric-shopping. If the orchestrator intends the sealed judged crop to be THE domain (it is the pixels the blind judges actually saw), the ruling is the same: pair03 fails at 0.473. what_would_make_this_verdict_wrong: MY M6 IMPLEMENTATION IS MINE. RI-VIS03 ships pseudocode, not code; I transcribed M2/M6/M7 into tools/visual/f4c-analyse.mjs --vis03 and the SKY_MASK step needed a gradient threshold I approximated with a Sobel-style magnitude. If my hue_offset is wrong, the hard fail falls. Two things argue it is not: six vendored modern-fidelity plates measured on the SAME code in the SAME session read 16-143 deg while ours reads 3.7, so the instrument separates the populations the item says it should; and the result agrees with what all five Protocol A r2 judges wrote in their own words. A re-implementation by another critic is the cheap way to falsify me.

MY LIT MASK COULD BE WRONG IF `__shadowMap(false)` DID NOT APPLY. It is enforced per frame and every material is marked needsUpdate, and the per-arm readback records `shadowMapEnabled` — but the strongest evidence is visual: the third panel of frames/pair03__BEFORE-sourcerevert__AFTER__AFTER-shadowmap-OFF.png is unmistakably a fully sunlit version of the same frame. If it had not applied, that panel would look like the middle one.

THE BEFORE ARM IS A TWO-LINE REVERT, NOT A CHECKOUT OF THE PARENT COMMIT. If F4 changed anything else that matters, my baseline is wrong. The diff at e9b30a82 touches four files; the two source files' changes are the recipe numbers, the `moon` field and one multiplication, and the null control being byte-identical across the two trees is the check that the refactor half is a no-op.
SOFTWARE RENDERING. Every capture of mine is SwiftShader. Absolute appearance claims would be void; every claim here is a differential.

notes.s52_null_control: Asking S52's question of prsv-dusk — could it have moved? From the FOUR NUMBERS, no: dusk-canopy's own key/sky/fill/env are byte-untouched, so as a control on the VALUES it is trivial. From the CODE, yes: the change also adds `moon: 1.0` to EXTERIOR_RIG, scales `moon` in resolveLightingRecipe(), and multiplies this.moon.intensity by `R.moon ?? 1` in sky.js. My live readback at 06:00 shows the moon at 0.31383 and IDENTICAL in both arms — so the moon path is genuinely exercised in that frame and returns exactly today's behaviour. A missing `?? 1`, a wrong default or an arm scaling the wrong directional would have moved it. It is a real leak check on the refactor and no evidence at all about the rebalance, and the builder presented it as the latter.
notes.what_the_live_scene_says: Readback at capture time, both arms, from tools/visual/f4c-critic.mjs. pairs01-04: sun 2.1 -> 6.3 (exactly x3), env 1.00 -> 0.35, MOON 0 IN BOTH — so `key_off` and `sun_off` are the same experiment there, measured rather than argued. pair05: sun 0.0126 in BOTH arms (the sun really is off at 19:30, which is the builder's whole reason for using key_off), moon 0.82 -> 2.952 (x3.6), env 0.75 -> 0.195. Hemisphere total 5.1248 -> 5.0011, which is the sky's own 0.4948 -> 0.3711 (x0.75) on top of 4.63 of cell-art hemisphere light that no recipe reaches — the arithmetic closes exactly.
notes.credit_where_it_is_due: This build's status file is the most honest one I have read in this repo. It leads with what it could not do, it reports a fail rather than choosing the view that passes, it names its own acceptance metric as defective and refuses to rewrite the bar it was measured against, it records a hypothesis its own arm refuted, and it wrote the measurement that refused dusk-canopy into the source file so the next reader does not re-derive it. Every number I could re-derive from its data reproduced exactly. My disagreements are with two descriptions and with what was not measured, not with its arithmetic or its candour.
